content.text: Vol expansion: hypovolemia, hemorrhage, septic shock (initial resuscitation), med diluent, ↓Na correction (cautiously)
Lrg vol infusion -> hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis.
**Avoid in pt w hypernatremia or hyperchloremia**
Preferred resuscitation fluid for trauma, burns, surgery, and sepsis
Lactate converted to bicarb by liver — may benefit acidotic pt
Dist throughout entire body once glucose is metabolized
Too much infusion -> hyponatremia and hyperglycemia
dextrose adds osmolarity but limited nutritional value
**Risk fluid overload, Not ideal for resuscitation**
Free water + lyte repletion, hypernatremia correction, maintenance fluids in normovolemic pt
Solution = hypotonic -> poss worsen cerebral edema
Severe Sx ↓Na, traumatic brain injury (TBI) w cerebral edema, herniation syndromes
given via central line or lrg peripheral IV
Too rapid Na correction -> risk osmotic demyelination syndrome (ODS/CPM)
5%: vol expansion: shock, cirrhosis (spont bacterial peritonitis), liver transplant
25%: hepatorenal syndrome, nephrotic syndrome, pull fluid from extravasc space
25% albumin pulls fluid into intravasc space — monitor for vol overload
